Brand: Luma Pantry

Luma Pantry is a direct-to-consumer meal kit service for working professionals who cook at home 3–5 nights a week. The brand sits between mass-market convenience (HelloFresh, Gousto) and premium aspirational cooking (Ottolenghi, Dishoom at-home kits). The positioning is "real cooking made frictionless" — not quick and easy, not cheffy performance, but genuinely good food that fits the actual shape of a busy evening.

Campaign objective: Drive new subscriber acquisition for the September "Back to Routine" season. Focus on lapsed home cooks who fell off during summer (takeaway drift) and working couples aged 28–40 who want to eat better but struggle to plan.

Products in scope: Weekly meal kit subscription (3 or 5 nights), First Box discount (40% off), optional recipe card postal add-on.

Budget: £15,000–£25,000 campaign budget.

Timeline: Campaign live from 8 September, runs 6 weeks. Follow-up retention sequence begins in week 4.

Channels: Instagram (primary acquisition), email (re-engagement and conversion), Meta paid social (retargeting lapsed subscribers), editorial content partnership (one food publication, TBC).

Audience: Working professionals, 28–40, London/Manchester/Edinburgh, household income £50k+. Cook 3–5 times per week. Main sensitivities: "too much faff", "ingredients I can't use", "feels like homework", "guilt if I miss a box". Not interested in: performative cooking content, influencer recipes, anything that feels like a diet brand.

Constraints: Cannot use any real customer names or photos without signed consent — use "scenario-based creative" only. No food waste guilt messaging. No "healthy eating" positioning (brand avoids wellness language). No scarcity countdown timers.

Open questions: First Box offer depth (40% or 50%?), editorial partner not confirmed, photography budget within overall limit.
